Traced it end to end. You don't lose it at one point — it's never captured at all. The author is absent at every layer of the comment path:

| Layer | What happens | File |
|---|---|---|
| Middleware | `AuthMiddleware` **does** run on `POST /articles/:slug/comments` and sets `req.user` — identity is available | `article.module.ts:28` |
| Controller | `createComment(@Param('slug'), @Body('comment'))` — **no `@User('id')` param**, so `req.user` is never read | `article.controller.ts:77` |
| DTO | `CreateCommentDto` declares only `body` | `dto/create-comment.ts:2` |
| Service | `addComment()` does `comment.body = commentData.body` and nothing else | `article.service.ts:104-105` |
| Entity | `Comment` has `id`, `body`, `article` — **no `author` relation**, so the table has no `authorId` column | `comment.entity.ts:5-15` |
| Response | `findComments()` returns `article.comments` raw; the `Comment` interface behind `CommentsRO` only declares `body` | `article.interface.ts:3-5`, `article.service.ts:167` |

The first concrete drop is `article.controller.ts:77` — that's where known identity gets thrown away, and it's the odd one out: `create()` (line 52) and `favorite()` (line 94) both take `@User('id') userId`. But fixing only that gets you nothing, because `addComment` has nowhere to put the value.

Two knock-on effects worth knowing:

- **Existing rows can't be backfilled.** There's no `authorId` column, so every comment already in the DB has no recoverable author — the data was never written, not just never returned.
- **This blocks the ownership work.** `CURRENT_FOCUS.md:11-13` lists 403s on `DELETE /articles/:slug/comments/:id` and already notes the missing relation; `auth.md:60` confirms there's no author to compare the caller against.

The fix is a four-layer change: `@ManyToOne(() => UserEntity)` on the entity, `@User('id')` on the controller, a `userId` arg through `addComment`, and adding `author` to the response shape. Since the DB runs `synchronize: true` (`schema.md:6-9`), the column appears on boot — no migration file. One design question you'd need to settle: whether the relation is eager, since `article.comments` is already `{eager: true}`, so eager-loading authors adds a join to every single article load.

Want me to implement it?
